title: Possible memory leak / retained memory after closing RDP sessions
author: Buster-de
body_snippet:
During testing with `mRemoteNG-nightly-20260909-v1.83.0-00cd029-x64.msi` to validate issue #179, I noticed that opening an RDP connection increases the process's memory usage (active private working set) by roughly 300 MB in my environment.

After opening and closing several RDP connections, including closing their tabs and panels, the allocated memory does not appear to be released.

How to reproduce
* Open and close several RDP sessions.

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Thank you for running it and for pasting the whole series — the raw numbers are what exposed two things, both ours.

**The script's verdict was wrong.** "No accumulation" over a process that went from 49 MB to 1036 MB is nonsense. An RDP desktop painting swings private bytes by hundreds of MB from one second to the next; the script's peak-and-trough guess turned your four or five sessions into fifteen and averaged the noise. Your numbers show substantial retained-memory growth: 274 MB after the first close to 1,274 MB after the fourteenth, another 1,000 MB across 13 sessions. comments.snippet:
This issue was closed by a commit word on 1 October. That close is not a finding that the retained memory is fixed.

What we can say: in our lab a closed RDP session kept about 1 MB of private memory, on the order of the other report of about 4 MB per close, and above the empty mstscax control. We have not reproduced a jump of hundreds of megabytes on the first close. The builds those reports were taken on do not have the later per-close fields.
